name: sources
purpose: The sources a generative AI response drew on (ChatGPT's Sources, Cloudscape's sources section, AI Elements Sources): a small `Sources` pill with the overlapping marks of up to three cited sources that opens, in place, a `Popover` listing every source. Sources the answer searched but did not cite (`cited: false`) are listed under More, after the Citations. The pill ends the message's action row (`ChatMessage.Actions` `#trailing`), on the same line as the actions. Each mark is the site's favicon (`image`), its icon, or its first letter on a colour of its own, so three sources never look alike.
useWhen: A response is grounded in documents, pages or records the reader may want to open or verify.
avoidWhen: Related links that the response did not use → `help-panel` links or a plain list.
A single source → cite it inline with `Citation`; a list of one is noise.
related: `citation` — the inline chip whose numbers point at these items.
`streaming-response` — renders the citations; pass it the same items.
`chat-message` — the pill goes in the `#trailing` slot of `ChatMessage.Actions`, after the icon actions.
`popover` — the anchored panel the pill opens.
bestPractices: Order items as the response first cites them, so `[1]` is item 1; put uncited items (`cited: false`) last so the numbers stay aligned.
Use the page title as the title and the site's own name as `site` (`Azion`, `GitHub`); without `site` the host of `href` shows.
Pass `publisher` and `publishedAt` when you have them.
Keep the panel closed by default; the inline citations are the primary path.
Give `image` the site's favicon URL when the app has one (from the search tool's result); otherwise `icon` for a site in the icon set, or nothing for the lettered mark.

props.name: items
props.doc: The sources behind the response, in citation order; item `n` is what `[n]` points at.

props.name: title
props.doc: Label of the pill that opens the panel. Empty shows `Sources` and names the pill with the count (`3 sources`).
